open_points.subject: owner session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and scope enforce this, especially since browser cookies are scoped by host and path rather than by origin or port, and is the cookie Secure on locally reached HTTP?
options: Host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure always, with a path limited to the owner interface
Host-only and HttpOnly, Secure only for remote HTTPS, with a path limited to the owner interface
Host-only and HttpOnly with Path=/, relying on server-side route authorization
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, Secure wherever HTTPS is used, and limit its path to the owner interface.

open_points.subject: owner session teardown
open_points.text: “The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart”
open_points.question: When an expiry is first detected, must Registry immediately remove the session and all pending confirmation/upload state and clear the browser cookie, or may invalid session state and the cookie remain until later cleanup?
options: Remove all session state and expire the cookie on the first request that detects the end
Refuse the request but retain state until periodic cleanup, while clearing the cookie
Only mark the session invalid and leave both state and cookie until their natural cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Remove all session state and return an expired cookie on the first detected end.

open_points.subject: ordering concurrent owner-session requests
open_points.text: “applied one at a time, in the order they reach the session”
open_points.question: What event establishes the total order when concurrent requests arrive together: socket receipt, completion of authentication, acquisition of a session lock, or another defined linearization point?
options: Order when Registry assigns a monotonic receipt sequence before session checks
Order when each request acquires the session-state lock
Permit either order for requests whose arrival order cannot be distinguished
open_points.default_guess: Use acquisition of the session-state lock as the observable linearization point.

open_points.subject: confirmation binding
open_points.text: “its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never as the values themselves”
open_points.question: Which inputs belong to each confirmed action, how are absent values, collections and text encoded and ordered, and which digest algorithm produces the binding?
options: Define a canonical typed serialization and a fixed cryptographic digest for every confirmed action
Digest the request body's exact bytes
Bind only the explicitly named target and revision/version, with action-specific extra values
open_points.default_guess: Define an action-specific ordered field list, canonical typed encoding, and SHA-256 digest.

open_points.subject: import with no selected projects
open_points.text: “the owner picks any subset of its projects”
open_points.question: May the owner confirm an empty selection, thereby writing the migration closure and permanently closing the one import without importing anything?
options: Refuse confirmation unless at least one project is picked
Accept an empty import and write the closure
Accept it as a no-op without writing the closure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse confirmation unless at least one project is picked.

open_points.subject: import mapping contents
open_points.text: “the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display name and alias each will arrive under”
open_points.question: Must the mapping expose every imported fact the owner is approving—including object values, customer link, retained instants, pointer references, statuses and versions—or only the named summary?
options: Show every fact that the transaction will store
Show only the named summary and validation findings
Show all personal data and identities, but summarize retained history fields
open_points.default_guess: Show every fact that will be stored, grouped by project, customer, room and pointer.

open_points.subject: import object mapping
open_points.text: “An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers”
open_points.question: How are the required embedded Object address, optional kind and characteristics derived from the v1 project, validated, and shown in the mapping before the project is stored?
options: Map declared v1 project fields deterministically and show the resulting Object
Require the owner to supply all Object values during mapping
Import only the address and leave optional Object values absent
open_points.default_guess: Map the v1 address into the embedded Object, leave unavailable optional values absent, and show the complete result.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm is used, and is it computed over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonical parsed representation?
options: SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes
SHA-256 over a canonical serialization of parsed data
A release-selected digest recorded with its algorithm identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: configuration validation
open_points.text: “each well formed”
open_points.question: What makes each location and secret well formed beyond the separately stated minimum secret length and path checks?
options: Define exact encodings and path syntax for every item
Treat any byte string of sufficient length as a secret and any resolvable absolute path of the required kind as a location
Leave well-formedness to the configuration loader
open_points.default_guess: Accept arbitrary secret bytes of sufficient length and require absolute, resolvable paths of the stated file or directory kind.

open_points.subject: unknown configuration items
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other”
open_points.question: What container or namespace is examined for unknown items, so ordinary process environment variables are not silently treated either as forbidden Registry configuration or as ignored unknown configuration?
options: A dedicated configuration file whose complete schema is checked
A Registry-prefixed environment-variable namespace, ignoring all other variables
The entire process environment, rejecting every unrecognized variable
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated Registry configuration namespace and reject unknown keys only inside it.

open_points.subject: startup probe cleanup
open_points.text: “A failed start leaves no file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run removes with the other temporary files.”
open_points.question: At what startup step is a leftover probe identified and removed, and does inability to remove it fail the next start or merely leave it for a backup run?
options: Remove stale probes before the new writability probe and fail startup if removal fails
Attempt removal but continue if a new probe can be created and removed
Leave startup unchanged and let the next backup run remove it
open_points.default_guess: Remove stale probes before testing writability and fail startup if any cannot be removed.

open_points.subject: configuration secret confidentiality
open_points.text: “configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and the Registry process”
open_points.question: Is Registry required to verify ownership and permissions of a file holding secrets before serving, or is this entirely an unchecked host-administration guarantee?
options: Verify file ownership and refuse group/world-readable secret configuration
Treat permissions as an explicit host-administration responsibility and perform no check
Verify permissions only where the configuration source exposes meaningful ownership metadata
open_points.default_guess: Verify restrictive ownership and permissions when using a file, while treating non-file configuration security as host administration.

open_points.subject: backup cryptography
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation rule, key interpretation or derivation, and file format are required?
options: Fix an authenticated-encryption scheme and versioned envelope format in State 2
Let each release choose and record an algorithm identifier in the backup
Use encryption without a normative algorithm or envelope
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned envelope with a random nonce and a fixed modern authenticated-encryption scheme.

open_points.subject: backup metadata integrity
open_points.text: “It records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key”
open_points.question: Are the readable metadata cryptographically authenticated with the encrypted store, and what prevents alteration of the instant, release, sequence number or key digest?
options: Authenticate all cleartext metadata as associated data
Place a signed or keyed authentication tag over the metadata separately
Leave metadata unauthenticated and trust the backup directory
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the complete cleartext header as associated data of the encrypted payload.

open_points.subject: overlapping scheduled backup runs
open_points.text: “Runs never overlap.”
open_points.question: If the previous day's run is still active at the next 03:00 UTC, is that day's run skipped, queued to start when the old run finishes, or does it cancel or fail the old run?
options: Skip the new run with a diagnostic
Queue exactly one run to start immediately after the active run
Cancel the active run and start the scheduled one
open_points.default_guess: Skip the overlapping run, record a diagnostic, and try again at the following 03:00.

open_points.subject: backup retention deadline
open_points.text: “it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before” and “an erasure reaches the backups at most 30 days after it”
open_points.question: Because cleanup runs only daily and deletes only backups already older than 30 days, a backup can remain for almost 31 days after an erasure; is the guarantee 30 days, up to the next successful daily run after 30 days, or must deletion occur at the exact deadline?
options: Guarantee deletion no later than 30 days after erasure, requiring earlier cutoff or independent scheduling
Retain for 30 days plus up to one successful-run interval
Define 30 days as 30 scheduled backup cycles rather than elapsed time
open_points.default_guess: State the bound as 30 days plus up to one daily-run interval, extended further by failed or missed runs.

open_points.subject: newest-backup status in owner interface
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup, read from the kept backups.”
open_points.question: Before the next cleanup run, how does the interface treat a kept-prefix file with malformed or tampered metadata, or a kept backup that cannot be opened with an available key?
options: Ignore invalid files and show the newest structurally valid kept backup
Report backup status unavailable if any kept-prefix file is invalid
Show the newest header that parses, without decrypting or rechecking it
open_points.default_guess: Ignore invalid kept-prefix files, report them diagnostically, and show the newest structurally valid kept backup.

open_points.subject: agent project-set check
open_points.text: “(2) for agent authority, the session and its set” and “(6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the set”
open_points.question: Is failure because a project is outside the agent session's set a stage 2 authorization failure or a stage 6 lifecycle failure?
options: Stage 2 only, hiding all existence, value and lifecycle checks
Stage 6 after record existence, values and version checks
Check at both stages but require the same not-found answer
open_points.default_guess: Treat it exclusively as stage 2 so every later fact remains hidden.

open_points.subject: multiple failures within authentication stage
open_points.text: “for the owner, a valid owner session … then for a change its CSRF value … then a confirmation value” and “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them.”
open_points.question: When the owner session is invalid, Registry cannot determine whether supplied CSRF and confirmation values are bound to that session; should it report only the session failure or also report the dependent checks as failures?
options: Stop at the first dependent check within the stage
Report every independently evaluable failure but skip checks requiring unavailable state
Report session, CSRF and confirmation failures together
open_points.default_guess: Report every independently evaluable failure and skip dependent checks when their session state is unavailable.

open_points.subject: multiple missing records in stage 3
open_points.text: “that every record the action names exists — its target and any it newly names” and “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them.”
open_points.question: Must Registry look up and disclose every missing named record in one answer, or may a dependency such as a missing pointer or project stop lookups whose identities can only be derived from it?
options: Aggregate all checks whose identifiers are present in the request and skip dependent lookups
Always return only the first missing record
Require every operation to define its own aggregation and dependency order
open_points.default_guess: Aggregate independently named records and skip checks that depend on a missing record.

open_points.subject: pending confirmation lifecycle in M11
open_points.text: M11 says the pending confirmation is “cleared when used”; A13 also says an expired pending confirmation is cleared by a submission “whatever value it gives.”
open_points.question: Does clearing an expired confirmation count as use for M11, or must M11 explicitly include expiry-triggered clearing as a separate transition?
options: Define use broadly to include an expired submission that clears it
Amend the lifecycle to say cleared when used or when an expired submission is received
Do not clear an expired confirmation unless the submitted value matches it
open_points.default_guess: Treat expiry-triggered clearing as a separate explicit transition in M11.
